A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TRACE research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original TRACE experiments on detoxification, character personalization, and political/nontoxic composition, alongside classifier and efficiency analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original TRACE experiments and reports additional transformation-ablation and HMM-training-checkpoint results.

M1.justification: HMM distillation, factorized classifiers, log-MSE fitting, forward/backward EAP computation, probability transformations, and attribute composition remain unchanged. Decoding-time transformation receives clearer methodological documentation in v2 but was already described and evaluated in v1.

E1.justification: Both retain detoxification and political/nontoxic generation using RealToxicityPrompts, RoleBench personalization, and News Category data for political-classifier training. Revised configurations and supplementary analyses do not establish additional task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains DAPT, GeDi, FUDGE, DExperts, PPLM, MuCoLa, PPO, and Quark for GPT-2, plus DPO for both language models. Prompting and neural-classifier comparators also remain. Changes concern TRACE ablations; the newly discussed NADO is not evaluated.

E3.justification: V1 Appendix B specifies 4096 HMM states generally; v2 Appendix C specifies 256 for personalization while retaining 4096 for detoxification/composition. The HMM-quality evaluation also changes from a 1M-versus-10M training-sample comparison to training-checkpoint evaluation using validation likelihood and toxicity. These are substantive reported configuration and design changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds an untransformed TRACE control in Table 2 and replaces the training-data-volume HMM ablation with a likelihood/toxicity trajectory in Figure 5. It removes the political and composite decoding-transformation variants and v1's per-character training-time/quality analysis. Factorizability and fluency-control analyses remain, so supporting analyses are substantially revised rather than simply relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version provides seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, or specified significance-testing procedures. Point-estimate reporting and the shaded fit in Figure 3 remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Headline detoxification scores and relocated entropy/GPT-4 scores are retained. V2 adds no-transformation toxicity results of 0.353 average maximum and 0.196 probability, adds HMM-checkpoint results, and changes the inference ratio from 1.1 to 1.2. It removes the low-data Gemma HMM and two transformed-composition result rows. Figure 4 changes role scores and contains 85 plotted points versus 76 in v1, despite retaining the 76-character description; these are not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The EAP derivation, HMM recursions, factorization assumptions, composition assumption, and complexity bounds are retained. Removing v1's redundant integration equations and renumbering the remaining equations do not change the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion revise the claimed decoding overhead from approximately 10% to 20%. The central claims of tractable control, strong detoxification, rapid personalization, and compositional generation remain.

C2.justification: V2 removes v1's explicit qualification that politics and nontoxicity were not significantly anticorrelated in RealToxicityPrompts. It emphasizes successful low-probability fitting in the transformation discussion and connects HMM effectiveness to improving validation likelihood rather than training-data volume. The principal expressivity limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access link and discloses latent-variable initialization, mini-batch EM, batch size 4096, 50 epochs, and a linear step-size schedule from 1 to 0. These expand implementation documentation without proving an optimizer change. Conversely, v1's 7500-prompt composition count and explicit non-batched timing condition are omitted.

R1.justification: V2 adds Sato (1999), Peharz et al. (2020), and Zhang et al. (2025) for HMM training, removes the Gemma Team reference, and explicitly discusses the already-cited NADO. The central positioning against discriminator, sampling, and logical-control approaches remains unchanged; publication-metadata updates do not represent new works.

P1.justification: Related work, classifier explanations, and much of the experimental narrative are substantially condensed and rewritten. Redundant integration exposition is removed, a new Appendix B groups relocated evaluations, subsequent appendices are reorganized, and an impact statement is added.

P2.justification: V2 restructures Table 1 and separates transformation ablations, relocates entropy and GPT-4 tables to the appendix, and merges training/inference tables. It removes the role-training scatter plot, adds an HMM-quality plot, redraws Figure 4 with expanded axes, and revises several figure sizes, placements, and captions.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility through its code link and HMM training specifications and strengthens transformation analysis with an untransformed control. However, it removes direct per-character timing evidence and transformed-composition results, while Figure 4 introduces an unresolved mismatch between 85 plotted points and the stated 76 characters. These documentation and diagnostic gains coexist with losses of supporting evidence and reporting inconsistencies, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
